steps.what: Submit device, version and symptom or install
Read the current procedure for that device
Draft troubleshooting procedures from the request

loop.input: request fields and the current procedure
loop.output: steps that cite the device id and the symptom or install type
loop.check: Device id and symptom or install type match the request
loop.stop: One draft; stop a step that has no device id
loop.why_not_simpler: The safe order of steps is not a fixed table

steps.what: Walk through the steps with the operator
File the signed procedure version
Try one step and report a gap

tasks.design: The operator submits device id, software version and either an install type or a symptom code on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded draft in {DOCS} writes procedure steps that must cite those fields. The architect walks through the steps with the operator, signs one version, and only that version is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures were rewritten from memory after each fault, so the steps did not match the device that was actually in the rack.
tasks.enabler_now: Device id, software version and symptom code can be required fields, and a draft can be rejected when it cites something else.
tasks.still_hard: The walkthrough still finds steps that are true on paper and wrong on the device.
tasks.human_edge: The architect decides which steps are safe to publish and which stay as a warning.

ambition.what: Update the procedure in the same week as the fault, not at the next audit

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to retyping known steps. The architect can refuse a procedure that names no device id.

reach.task: Follow the signed procedure on the next fault
reach.learn: Which procedure version is current and which steps failed the walkthrough

evidence.claim: A communications procedure in a mid-size firm is a document plus a short walkthrough. The hard part is the step that is wrong on the device.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong. That is the title and the device id, not the procedure body.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends when a signed procedure version is filed. Running it on a live fault is later work.
Input contract: device id, software version, install type or symptom code, owner. Producer is the network operator. If both install type and symptom code are empty, no draft is started.
Use the document store's own template before custom code. The meeting prior fits the walkthrough and is kept. Template upkeep is incremental, not zero.
unknowns: Which device families have no procedure template.
Who may sign when the architect is absent.
Whether software version is on the inventory or only on the device.
research_questions: What share of procedures cite a device id that is no longer in service?
How often does the walkthrough delete a drafted step?

already_counted.description: Architect deletes drafted steps that are unsafe
Walkthrough time stays with the architect

incremental.description: Add a template when a new device family arrives
Operators resubmit a symptom code the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: procedure version signed in this walkthrough

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes symptom codes are free text, so the draft rarely matches and the architect writes the steps. The high case assumes coded cases draft cleanly, but the walkthrough and the sign-off still happen every time. Live fault repair is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Join the upgrade and record the tests

steps.what: State the upgrade scope and the sites
Draft the integration test list

loop.input: scope fields and the test template
loop.output: test rows that each cite a site id
loop.check: Every test row cites a site id from the scope
loop.stop: One pass; drop a row with no site id
loop.why_not_simpler: Pass criteria differ by change type and are not a fixed table

steps.what: Attend the upgrade and cutover meetings
Join the on-site install and test
Rack the hardware for this window
Sign the cutover version
Apply the signed cutover on the network

tasks.design: The service owner submits project id, sites and the change type on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded list in {DOCS} drafts integration checks from those fields only. Meetings, the on-site test and the cutover stay with people. The architect signs one cutover version, and the live change uses only that version on the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Upgrade scope arrived as slides and mail, so the test list could not be checked against a site id.
tasks.enabler_now: Project id, site and change type can be fields, and a test row can be required to cite one of them.
tasks.still_hard: The cutover on a live site, and the meetings around it, do not become a template.
tasks.human_edge: The architect decides whether the test result is good enough to cut over, and applies that change by hand.
tasks.altitude: The test list takes less rewriting. Meetings, the site visit and the cutover do not move. The architect can refuse a cutover that has no signed version.

reach.task: Rack only the hardware named on the signed test list
reach.learn: Which cutover version is signed and which tests are still open

evidence.claim: Upgrade participation in a mid-size firm is meetings, a site visit and a test. Little of it is a repeated document.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so the cutover stays a person with a signed version.
Digest [S16] and [S18] say that for firms in scope the Dutch cyber duty of care includes patching and supply-chain measures. Whether this firm is in scope is separate.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task is participation in one upgrade, including the on-site test and the signed cutover. It is not the yearly portfolio review.
Input contract: project id, site, change type, vendor name, test owner. Producer is the service owner. A test row with no site id is not drafted.
The standardisation prior is that this work is not standard. Native project fields are used before custom code. An unattended cutover is out of scope.
unknowns: Who is allowed to touch production on the night.
Which tests the vendor runs and which the architect runs.
Whether this firm is in scope of the cyber duty of care.
research_questions: How many integration tests are repeated from the last upgrade unchanged?
How often is the first cutover rolled back?

already_counted.description: Architect edits test rows that do not match the site
Meeting time stays with the architect

incremental.description: Add a test row type when a new change type appears

approvals.approved_version: cutover version signed from these test notes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the scope is still slides, so the test list is written by hand and almost all time stays in meetings and on site. The high case assumes a clean scope form, but the meetings, the visit and the cutover are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Build a configuration prototype in the lab

steps.what: State the trial id, feature and constraint
Draft a candidate config from the trial

loop.input: trial fields and the lab template
loop.output: config note citing trial id and lab device id
loop.check: Trial id and lab device id match the form
loop.stop: One draft; return an empty note if the lab device id is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: Interface order varies by feature and is not a fixed merge

steps.what: Build the prototype on lab equipment
Run the lab checks and record results
Decide if the prototype is fit to keep
File the signed lab result

tasks.design: The service owner submits a trial id, feature and constraint on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts a candidate config that cites only those fields. The architect builds it on lab gear in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, runs the checks, and signs the lab result. The prototype is not copied to the live network in this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Trial notes were free text, so a config could not be tied back to the feature under test.
tasks.enabler_now: Trial id, feature and constraint can be fields, and a lab device id can be kept separate from production device ids.
tasks.still_hard: Building the prototype and reading a failed check still take the architect's hands.
tasks.human_edge: The architect decides whether the lab result is fit to keep or must be torn down.

ambition.what: Close a failed lab prototype in the same week, instead of leaving it running

tasks.altitude: The config note takes less rewriting. The bench time stays. The architect can refuse to keep a prototype that has no trial id.

reach.task: Decide whether to ask for a live design later
reach.learn: Which trial id passed and which lab device must be torn down

evidence.claim: Prototype time in a mid-size firm sits on the lab bench and the config note. The meeting prior overstates a task that is mostly the build.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so this task stops at the lab and does not push the config live.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends at a signed lab result. Promoting the config to production is a later change with its own approval.
Input contract: trial id, feature, constraint, lab device id, interface. Producer is the service owner. A missing lab device id stops the draft.
The meetings prior is high. For this task the time is the lab screen, the config and a short fit decision. Use the lab gear's own config export before custom code.
unknowns: Which lab devices are isolated from production.
Who may power a lab device when the architect is away.
research_questions: What share of prototypes are torn down without a written result?
How often does the first config fail its own checks?

already_counted.description: Architect corrects a config note that misses the constraint
Bench time on the prototype stays with the architect

incremental.description: Extend the lab template when a new feature family is trialled

approvals.approved_version: lab result version signed for this trial id
the same signed lab result version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the trial arrives as a sentence, so the draft is empty and the architect still builds from scratch. The high case assumes a clean trial form, but the build, the checks and the fit decision stay manual. No live change is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose a link size for the volume

steps.what: Read current size and the threshold
State the volume the site must carry
Draft two size options with a rollback

loop.input: link row, volume and the threshold table
loop.output: two options each citing one link id and a rollback
loop.check: Each option cites a link id on the size view and a rollback size
loop.stop: If the link id is missing, return an empty note and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Which option the business can afford is not a fixed rule

steps.what: Choose the size and the rollback
Apply the signed size on the live link
Record the new size on the inventory

tasks.design: The capacity note and the volume the service owner needs are rows on a {BI} view, with link id and target. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts two size options from the threshold table, each with a rollback. The architect signs one option. The live size change on the {OPS_SYSTEM} is done by hand and only for that signed version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Volume asks and counter exports did not share a link id, so a size option could not show which hour it used.
tasks.enabler_now: Link id, current size, volume and threshold can be one row, and a rollback can be a required field on the decision.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong size on a live link drops traffic, and the volume the business will accept is not a formula.
tasks.human_edge: The architect picks the size and the rollback, and applies the change only after signing it.

ambition.what: Resize a link when it crosses the threshold, not only in the yearly plan

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to rebuilding the numbers. The decision and the live change stay. The architect can block a change that has no rollback.

reach.task: Confirm the volume the new size must carry
reach.learn: Which link ids have a signed size and which are still on the old size

evidence.claim: Sizing a link in a mid-size firm is a volume judgement and then a careful change. The numbers can be prepared. The change cannot be left unattended.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so the size change stays with the architect on a signed version.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. The volume view uses link counters, not a person's traffic.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task runs from a volume need to a signed size applied on that link, or a decision not to change it.

Input contract: link id, current size, requested volume, threshold, rollback size. Producer of the volume is the service owner. Producer of the counters is the monitoring export. A row with no link id is not drafted.
Use the monitoring view's own threshold before custom code. The live change is manual even after the signature.
unknowns: Whether a size change needs a carrier order rather than a local command.
Who may apply a change when the architect is away.
Which links have no current size in the inventory.
research_questions: What share of size changes are rolled back?
How often is the requested volume already inside the current size?

already_counted.description: Architect edits an option that lacks a real rollback
Hands-on size change stays with the architect

incremental.description: Update the threshold table when a new link type is added
Service owners correct a volume that was sent in the wrong unit

approvals.approved_version: size and rollback signed for this link id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes volume still arrives as mail and many links have no id, so both options are written by hand. The high case assumes clean rows, but the decision and the live change stay manual. Carrier lead time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Procedure text and lab notes take less rewriting. Upgrade meetings, on-site tests and the choice of link size stay with the architect.
reach: Network operators follow a signed procedure instead of asking for the steps again.
Vendor engineers receive the test list and the cutover version before they rack hardware.
skills_to_grow: Write a procedure step so it names a device id and a stop condition.
Keep a lab prototype off the live network until a later signed change.
State a size change as a link id, a target and a rollback.
role.ambitious_version: A new circuit opens from a signed procedure, a lab note that passed its checks, and a size decision that names the rollback.
